candidates.lead: Rarely-seen images from what proved to be the iconic band's penultimate show surface 40 years on
candidates.evidence_text: Manchester's Free Trade Hall has a special place in music history, as the venue - now a hotel - hosted some landmark moments It was where an electric guitar-wielding Bob Dylan famously faced an accusation of "Judas!" from a disgruntled folk fan , where a Sex Pistols show that inspired some of the city's most famous bands and the legendary Factory Records and where rock giants Kiss made their UK debut And it was where The Smiths, one of Manchester's most iconic bands, played what would prove to be their final farewell to the city on 30 October 1986 Forty years on, rarely-seen photos of the show, taken by then-student Alison Bell show what she said was a "dramatic" and "amazing" night Bell, who had been drawn to Manchester by its music scene as a student and went on to have a successful career in music promotion, said she had been desperate to see the band and the Free Trade Hall show was "the first opportunity I had to see them" Formed by singer Morrissey and guitarist Johnny Marr in 1982, the band were at the peak of their powers at the show, riding high on the success of their third long-player, The Queen Is Dead, which would go on to become widely-regarded as one of the greatest albums of all time

candidates.lead: The prosecution has been outlining its case against nine men accused of abusing an unconscious woman
candidates.evidence_text: This past week prosecutors have been outlining their case against a group of nine men - including a paramedic, children's football coach and taxi driver - who allegedly raped or abused a woman after she had been drugged by her husband The husband, who cannot be named to protect his wife's legal right to anonymity, had already pleaded guilty to 62 offences against her committed at the home they shared in the Stockport area of Greater Manchester Four other men have also admitted sexual offences against her, but the remaining defendants deny all charges and are on trial at Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court Louise Oakley KC, lead counsel for the prosecution, has told the jury that both the husband and the other men were leading "double lives" while secretly fulfilling their "barbaric fantasies" The husband's own abuse against the woman, in her sixties, is believed to have begun in 2004 before he began inviting strangers he met on online chatrooms, swinging websites and messaging apps to join him from about 2023 Here the BBC summarises the allegations against each man standing trial

candidates.lead: Manchester's Free Trade Hall has a special place in music history, as the venue - now a hotel - hosted some landmark moments It was where an electric guitar-wielding Bob Dylan famously faced an accusation of "Judas!" from a disgruntled folk fan , where a Sex Pistols show that ins
candidates.evidence_text: Manchester's Free Trade Hall has a special place in music history, as the venue - now a hotel - hosted some landmark moments It was where an electric guitar-wielding Bob Dylan famously faced an accusation of "Judas!" from a disgruntled folk fan , where a Sex Pistols show that inspired some of the city's most famous bands and the legendary Factory Records and where rock giants Kiss made their UK debut And it was where The Smiths, one of Manchester's most iconic bands, played what would prove to be their final farewell to the city on 30 October 1986 Forty years on, rarely-seen photos of the show, taken by then-student Alison Bell show what she said was a "dramatic" and "amazing" night Bell, who had been drawn to Manchester by its music scene as a student and went on to have a successful career in music promotion, said she had been desperate to see the band and the Free Trade Hall show was "the first opportunity I had to see them" Formed by singer Morrissey and guitarist Johnny Marr in 1982, the band were at the peak of their powers at the show, riding high on the success of their third long-player, The Queen Is Dead, which would go on to become widely-regarded as one of the greatest albums of all time

View 6 Images Eccles Add to preferred sources News Charlotte Hall Local Democracy Reporter 16:40, 08 Nov 2026 It’s just past 4PM on a Thursday in Eccles, and people are fighting in the street. A brawl spills out onto the pavement outside a pub, and a drunk man is headbutted to the ground City Mayor Paul Dennett attempts to intervene. He’s out on a ‘walkabout’ with the M.E.N. and ward councillor and deputy mayor coun Mike McCusker to discuss the upcoming regeneration of Eccles town centre. It’s a major 15-year multi-billion-pound plan that could completely rejuven “So, there are some problems with anti-social behaviour around here,” coun McCusker says, deadpan, as we watch the city mayor pick the bleeding man off the floor. “The plan is to change that, too.” View 6 Images Councillor Mike McCusker (left) and City Mayor Paul Dennett (right) in Eccles town centre The project, which is due to be approved by council bosses at a cabinet meeting next week, includes new green and community spaces, and 1,300 new homes across a number of low and mid-rise buildings, alongside a smaller number of tower blocks up to 12 storeys high

It happened at the supermarket's branch on Silk Street, off Manchester Road on the outskirts of the town centre, on Saturday afternoon (November 7) Police received a report of a concern for welfare for a woman inside the store, a Greater Manchester Police (GMP) spokesperson said. Shoppers described them being treated first by staff and then paramedics when they arrived Others said they were told to leave the store and vacate the car park to allow the emergency services to deal with the incident. candidates.evidence_text: Remembrance M60 turned into stunning ‘Ring of Red’ by hundreds of bikers for Remembrance Sunday The Ring of Red Ride returned for another year View 16 Images 1 of 16 The Ring of Red on the M60 (Image: Jason Roberts /Manchester Evening News) Comments News Ramazani Mwamba News reporter 17:30, 08 Nov 2026 Updated 17:31, 08 Nov 2026 The thick blanket of fog that had caused chaos on Greater Manchester Roads had cleared up just in time for hundreds of bikers to embark on their annual ride around the M60 to mark Remembranc The motorway was a sea of red this afternoon for this year's Ring of Red Ride today (November 8). The ride, which began at the Birch services on the M62 at around 1pm, saw the group make a near 36-mile circuit around the M60 to create the visually striking sight A community-minded event, this year's ride was set up to raise money for the Heywood's Veteran Association while paying respects to the fallen servicemen of past and present Almost every footbridge found on the M60 was littered with residents who had come out to show their appreciation to the riders who responded in kind with waves, beeping their horn or flashing their headlights Bikers wore bright red t-shirts on top of their gear with the aim of the event to form a massive popular around Manchester when viewed from above

A brawl spills out onto the pavement outside a pub, and a drunk man is headbutted to the ground City Mayor Paul Dennett attempts to intervene. He’s out on a ‘walkabout’ with the M.E.N. and ward councillor and deputy mayor coun Mike McCusker to discuss the upcoming regeneration of Eccles town centre. It happened at the supermarket's branch on Silk Street, off Manchester Road on the outskirts of the town centre, on Saturday afternoon (November 7) Police received a report of a concern for welfare for a woman inside the store, a Greater Manchester Police (GMP) spokesperson said. Shoppers described them being treated first by staff and then paramedics when they arrived Others said they were told to leave the store and vacate the car park to allow the emergency services to deal with the incident. candidates.evidence_text: Salford 'The only thing that works in our favour is we are all white, so we are not the obvious target' HMOs have been the targets of protest and vandalism, but they are a lifeline for some people amid spiralling rents and a shortage of social housing Add to preferred sources News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 07:20, 08 Nov 2026 For 14 years, Sean* has called Salford home. He is 32 years old and has built up a good career in the city Like thousands of people in Greater Manchester, he lives in a house in multiple occupation (HMO). It's the only way he can afford to live in the city he loves It isn't the dream, but it works for Sean. Yet earlier in October, he received an email from the property management firm that looks after the HMO, telling him and his housemates to 'be safe' The email was prompted by a wave of anger, protest and vandalism targeting properties across Salford which were alleged to be HMOs accommodating asylum seekers. 'No HMO' was daubed on doors and walls in paint, while windows were bricked across the borough in October After the spate of attacks, the property managers told Sean and his housemates to report any concerns with police, but 'not to worry'. "When something like this comes up you are going to be more aware and agitated," he told the Manchester Evening News

candidates.evidence_text: Health Inside the striking Manchester building giving cancer patients a lifeline away from hospital Maggie's Manchester offers a slice of home comforts - and specialist support - for cancer patients and their loved ones when they need it most View 5 I Add to preferred sources News Bethan Finighan Science and Innovation Writer 07:21, 08 Nov 2026 There is little that can prepare someone for a cancer diagnosis. Life as you know it is flipped on its head - and patients and their loved ones are suddenly faced with confronting appoi But just a stone's throw from the Christie Hospital, where patients face the more clinical side of cancer care, is a place that feels more like home For 10 years, Maggie's Manchester has opened its doors to anyone affected by cancer, offering a different kind of support to people impacted by the disease There's absolutely nothing clinical about its striking building, designed by world-renowned architect and Stockport-born Lord Norman Foster. candidates.evidence_text: Greater Manchester Combined Authority Greater Manchester Combined Authority gave nearly £1m to anonymous figures in ‘secret’ payments A Manchester Evening News investigation has revealed that the Greater Manchester Combined Authority handed nearly £1m Add to preferred sources News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 07:20, 08 Nov 2026 Updated 11:32, 08 Nov 2026 The Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA) has given nearly £1m to anonymous beneficiaries since 2024 in a series of ‘secret’ payments The payments are listed in the GMCA’s public accounts to pay for consultancy work, professional fees, commissioned services, grants, and other things, but there is little detail on what specific services were provided and who the money went to A spokesperson for the GMCA said it redacts details of named individuals who receive payments when their name is not their trading name, which it said is 'in line with UK data protection legislation and local government transparency code of practice.' It added that its system is under 'continual review' The combined authority is facing calls for more transparency around where it is spending public money and what services were provided for the cash

View 6 Images Eccles Add to preferred sources News Charlotte Hall Local Democracy Reporter 16:40, 08 Nov 2026 It’s just past 4PM on a Thursday in Eccles, and people are fighting in the street. A brawl spills out onto the pavement outside a pub, and a drunk man is headbutted to the ground City Mayor Paul Dennett attempts to intervene. He’s out on a ‘walkabout’ with the M.E.N. and ward councillor and deputy mayor coun Mike McCusker to discuss the upcoming regeneration of Eccles town centre. It’s a major 15-year multi-billion-pound plan that could completely rejuven “So, there are some problems with anti-social behaviour around here,” coun McCusker says, deadpan, as we watch the city mayor pick the bleeding man off the floor. “The plan is to change that, too.” View 6 Images Councillor Mike McCusker (left) and City Mayor Paul Dennett (right) in Eccles town centre The project, which is due to be approved by council bosses at a cabinet meeting next week, includes new green and community spaces, and 1,300 new homes across a number of low and mid-rise buildings, alongside a smaller number of tower blocks up to 12 storeys high

The celebrations and traditions many take for granted can feel a world away when your c Yet even in the most difficult circumstances, small moments of happiness can make a huge difference. Shoppers described them being treated first by staff and then paramedics when they arrived Others said they were told to leave the store and vacate the car park to allow the emergency services to deal with the incident. candidates.evidence_text: Greater Manchester Combined Authority Greater Manchester Combined Authority gave nearly £1m to anonymous figures in ‘secret’ payments A Manchester Evening News investigation has revealed that the Greater Manchester Combined Authority handed nearly £1m Add to preferred sources News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 07:20, 08 Nov 2026 Updated 11:32, 08 Nov 2026 The Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA) has given nearly £1m to anonymous beneficiaries since 2024 in a series of ‘secret’ payments The payments are listed in the GMCA’s public accounts to pay for consultancy work, professional fees, commissioned services, grants, and other things, but there is little detail on what specific services were provided and who the money went to A spokesperson for the GMCA said it redacts details of named individuals who receive payments when their name is not their trading name, which it said is 'in line with UK data protection legislation and local government transparency code of practice.' candidates.evidence_text: Salford 'The only thing that works in our favour is we are all white, so we are not the obvious target' HMOs have been the targets of protest and vandalism, but they are a lifeline for some people amid spiralling rents and a shortage of social housing Add to preferred sources News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 07:20, 08 Nov 2026 For 14 years, Sean* has called Salford home. He is 32 years old and has built up a good career in the city Like thousands of people in Greater Manchester, he lives in a house in multiple occupation (HMO). It's the only way he can afford to live in the city he loves It isn't the dream, but it works for Sean. Yet earlier in October, he received an email from the property management firm that looks after the HMO, telling him and his housemates to 'be safe' The email was prompted by a wave of anger, protest and vandalism targeting properties across Salford which were alleged to be HMOs accommodating asylum seekers. 'No HMO' was daubed on doors and walls in paint, while windows were bricked across the borough in October After the spate of attacks, the property managers told Sean and his housemates to report any concerns with police, but 'not to worry'. "When something like this comes up you are going to be more aware and agitated," he told the Manchester Evening News

candidates.evidence_text: Courts Man left in coma after being hit by police car involved in 96mph chase tells rogue driver 'I blame you, not the cop' Cameron Grainger has been jailed months after the cop who was chasing him was handed a suspended prison sentence View 4 Images Add to preferred sources News John Scheerhout Crime reporter 10:22, 07 Nov 2026 Updated 10:22, 07 Nov 2026 A man left in a coma after being left with devastating injuries when he was hit by a police car involved in a 96mph chase blames the rogue driver the cop was pursuing The victim described how his life fell apart following the horror smash at around 3am on November 19, 2023. The officer behind the wheel of the Ford Kuga patrol car, PC Sam Lockley, was chasing a Seat Leon driven by Cameron Grainger through Rochdale The injured man spoke out as Grainger - who has a long history of motoring offences - was jailed for causing serious injury by dangerous driving at Manchester Crown Court. He said he blames the 25-year-old, even though it wasn't his car that hit him PC Lockley was handed a suspended prison sentence in February. He lost his job and his pension after being convicted of causing serious injury by dangerous driving. PC Lockley was also ordered to carry out 15 days of community service and banned from the road for two years The 41-year-old victim - a father-of-one and a forklift truck driver originally from Poland - described the devastating impact the crash has had on his life, leading to lifelong injuries and the breakdown of his family life

candidates.evidence_text: Wednesday 14 October 2026 at 10:33am Kirith Entwistle, the Labour MP for Bolton North East, has said she found the current court system "triggering" and had to watch her abuser "stare at her". Credit: UK Parliament A Labour MP has revealed that she is a victim of domestic abuse - Speaking in the Commons on October 13, Kirith Entwistle, who represents Bolton North East, described her experience of the current court system as "triggering", adding that she had to watch her abuser "stare at her" during a recent video hearing Ms Entwistle told her fellow MPs that she believes special measures - where victims are given protection or assistance in court - should be the standard in cases involving domestic abuse Examples of these measures could include screens, the ability to give evidence through a live link, or witnesses being able to be accompanied when giving evidence Measures to protect victims are included in the Courts and Tribunals Bill, which is currently going through Parliament Speaking during a debate on the bill, Ms Entwistle said: "It doesn’t matter how many times somebody tells me that they understand what I’m going through, or they acknowledge what I’ve been through, they really don’t unless they have lived it themselves or know somebody who has."

candidates.evidence_text: Monday 12 October 2026 at 5:22pm Credit: Family photo A police officer called to the home of a mother and her four children murdered hours later in an arson attack told a court she thought their killer was making "empty threats" and did not try to arrest him Pc Gemma Quinn told Bolton Coroner's Court she did not think it necessary to arrest Zak Bolland, 26, "there and then" after a 999 call from Michelle Pearson , 37, when he threatened her son and home on Jackson Street in Walkden , Salford Greater Manchester Police's (GMP) Pc Quinn said she planned to arrest Bolland when she was next on shift in two days' time But after she and a more junior colleague left Ms Pearson's home, Bolland returned less than three hours later to murder her and four of her children in a firebomb attack in the early hours of December 11 2017 The firebombing killed four of Michelle's children, Demi Pearson, 15, her brother Brandon, eight, and sisters Lacie, seven, and Lia, three Zak Bolland, 26, and David Worrall, 28, were both jailed for life the following year for the murders

Emergency services were called to Baguley Crescent, Middleton, at about 14:45 GMT on Saturday. The man died at the scene and his next of kin has been informed, a spokesman for Greater Manchester Police said. Neighbour Ian Walsh told the BBC: "The firefighters managed to get him out and then they did CPR on him outside the flat." Ian Walsh said people in the area were shocked by what had happened "There was a lot of smoke. We are all shocked," he added. The 73-year-old said crews including paramedics and an air ambulance tried to save the man. "It's very sad and bewildering that he died. "You don't expect it to happen opposite you. Visitors can also enjoy value-for-money funfair rides, with 95% The events have been planned to cater for a wide audience, including those who would prefer to attend an earlier, shorter, lower-noise display. Hosting three large-scale events across the city also helps reduce the environmental impact associated with multiple smaller community d A number of measures have been introduced to improve sustainability. Avoidable single-use plastics have been removed from all event sites, the pyrotechnics supplier uses sustainable packaging, and post-event litter picks will take place immediately after the celebrations. Local s In a bid to reduce food waste, any surplus food will, where possible, be redistributed through local charities and community projects in partnership with the Our Manchester Food Partnership

candidates.title: A breath of fresh air - new Clean Air Vision and Action Plan for Manchester unveiled
candidates.summary: New plans to boost air quality across Manchester between now and 2040 are being brought forward by the Council
candidates.reason: Visible repeat policy allows this item: concrete_story_change:declared. | Selection: Selected in city_watch shortlist before writing.

candidates.lead: New plans to boost air quality across Manchester between now and 2040 are being brought forward by the Council
candidates.evidence_text: New plans to boost air quality across Manchester between now and 2040 are being brought forward by the Council Manchester’s air quality has improved significantly in recent years due to investment in public transport and cycling and walking routes, cleaner vehicle technology including electric vehicles and stricter national emissions standards. The investment-led Greater Manchester Clean But while good progress has been made, the Council wants to go further because environmental air pollution remains a real health risk, especially for people in more disadvantaged communities or with existing health conditions who can be more vulnerable to its effects The Vision is simple: “Manchester will be a city where everyone can breathe cleaner air and live healthier lives.” Alongside it sits a headline action plan which will guide further measures to improve air quality across the city, based around four priorities Reduce people’s exposure to air pollution, prioritising the most vulnerable such as children and people with existing health conditions and communities where the potential health benefits are the greatest

If there is only one candidate nominated, then that candidate would be elected without contest. If more than one valid nomination is received, residents will go to the polls on Thursday 3 December 2026 to elect thei This is an opportunity for local people from all backgrounds to represent the interests of their community, raise issues that matter to residents and play a direct role in shaping the future of Royton North and the wider borough. Councillors represent the Council to the community Anyone wishing to stand for election can obtain a nomination pack from the Elections Office at the J.R.Clynes Building, Cultural Quarter, Greaves Street, Oldham, OL1 1AL, between 9am and 5pm, or they can be emailed on request by emailing election@oldham.gov.uk Completed nomination papers must be submitted in person and cannot be accepted by email, post, fax or any other electronic method. Papers can be delivered to the J.R.Clynes Building between 10am and 4pm and no later than 4pm on Friday 6 November

candidates.summary: Primary schools have been recognised for outstanding performance in the 2026 Summer Reading Challenge Read to the Beat

candidates.lead: Primary schools have been recognised for outstanding performance in the 2026 Summer Reading Challenge Read to the Beat

The awards recognise the borough’s success in horticulture, Following the outstanding gold achievement and scooping the overall Town Centres and City Centres title at the recent Royal Horticultural Society Britain in Bloom awards, Rochdale town centre’s horticulturists remained on their winning streak taking gold and best in category for Rochdale in Bloom treasurer Phil Massey also received an outstanding contribution award for his significant work supporting Rochdale’s success in both national and local efforts Baillie Street Quarter won the new Best Art in the Community award for outstanding artwork from the recent Common Walls International Mural Festival, organised by talented local artist Hayley Garner (Ayo). Rochdale BID also secured gold and won the Best Business Improvement Distr Hampton by Hilton hotel entered for the first time this year, taking gold and category winner, alongside a gold for nearby Norton Grange hotel in the Large Accommodation category

Lest we forget.” The Royal British Legion is holding its annual poppy appeal until Sunday 8 November 2026, raising money to support British servicemen and women and their families. candidates.evidence_text: Alfie and family with Wigan Council and Bethell representatives at the Wigan Road crossing An eleven-year-old boy concerned about the safety of a busy main road has seen his request for a pedestrian crossing become a reality A frequent visitor to Ashfield Park in Standish, Alfie Haywood grew increasingly concerned about crossing Wigan Road to access the park, particularly when he was on his way home from school or crossing with his family and younger sister Encouraged by his nan Ruth, Alfie wrote a letter to Wigan Council and Lisa Nandy MP to raise his concerns and request a safer crossing, resulting in a toucan crossing being installed, along with improved road infrastructure for motorists, pedestrians, and cyclists Alfie, a pupil at St Peter’s High School in Orrell, said: “The reason I wanted this crossing is because lots of children and families visit Ashfield Park, but because this is such a busy road, somebody might get run over and hurt, and a crossing will allow people to cross the roa “I feel very proud and confident that the council listened to my idea, and I would like other children to know that they can help their community to become a better place

Founded in 1597, Wigan Grammar School taught countless pupils in a history spanning almost four centuries and served as one of the town’s oldest continuously operating institu On Wednesday 28th October, a selection of former pupils, Wigan Council and Wrightington, Wigan, and Leigh NHS Trust representatives attended the unveiling of the blue plaque at the Thomas Linacre Centre, which housed the school from 1937 until its closure in 1972. Made using tr The central space is immersed in sanguine red. Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

Monumental in scale and ambition, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! is the artist’s most expansive presentation in the North to date Ai Weiwei is known around the world for his uncompromising artistic vision and political activism. From a childhood in exile to surviving secret detention in China, his remarkable life and career have led him to global prominence. Using sculpture, installation, film, photography In Button Up! , the artist turns his lens on two centuries of Chinese and British relations. Taking inspiration from Manchester, a city at the heart of the Industrial Revolution, Button Up! explores how historic systems of trade, empire and exploitation resonate in today’s humani Conceived as a total environment, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! brings together new and existing large-scale works on display in the UK for the first time. The monumental installation features porcelain, cotton, glass, bronze and even buttons and toy bricks. Each material contains a stor Both global and personal, the title Button Up! is a playful poke at the artist’s ongoing battle with censorship. History, power and empire collide in Button Up! – a major new exhibition from the world-leading artist and activist Ai Weiwei . Internationally renowned artist and activist Ai Weiwei turns his critical gaze to the last 200 years of global history with this major new exhibition. Monumental in scale and ambition, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! is the artist’s most expansive presentation in the North to date.. Ai Weiwei is known around the world for his uncompromising artistic vision and political activism. From a childhood in exile to surviving secret detention in China, his remarkable life and career have led him to global prominence. Using sculpture, installation, film, photography and architecture, his work is unafraid to ask urgent, critical questions.. In Button Up! , the artist turns his lens on two centuries of Chinese and British relations. Taking inspiration from Manchester, a city at the heart of the Industrial Revolution, Button Up! explores how historic systems of trade, empire and exploitation resonate in today’s humanitarian and political crises.. Conceived as a total environment, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! brings together new and existing large-scale works on display in the UK for the first time. The monumental installation features porcelain, cotton, glass, bronze and even buttons and toy bricks. Each material contains a story of human invention and consumption. Together, they paint a picture of globalisation.. Both global and personal, the title Button Up! is a playful poke at the artist’s ongoing battle with censorship. The exhibition also features the world premiere of a new body of work created especially for the vast spaces of the Warehouse – Eight-Nation Alliance Flags made from millions of buttons, as well as a new version of History Of Bombs made entirely from toy bricks.. The new commissions sit alongside large-scale works by the artist which are going on show in the UK for the first time: Law of the Journey (2017), a 47m long inflatable migrant boat containing hundreds of human figures and the artist’s largest artwork to date; Wang Family Ancestral Hall (2015), a Ming dynasty ancestral temple reassembled from 1,500 individual wooden pieces ; and La Commedia Umana (2017-21), a black Murano glass chandelier made up of over 2,000 pieces and weighing nearly 3 tonnes. Also on show is Circle of Animals/Zodiac Heads (2010), a re-envisioning of the twelve animals of the Chinese zodiac.. Button Up! immerses visitors in Ai Weiwei’s fearless interrogation of the forces past and present that drive today’s injustices – while championing art’s enduring power to challenge and inspire.. . . . “I’m not interested in making very big things just for the sake of it. But in Manchester, that wonderful Warehouse space calls for monumental work. Visiting the city for this exhibition – the birthplace of the Industrial Revolution – and reflecting on Britain’s global territorial expansion made me realise I had to explore that history and understand how it connects to the forces driving today’s wars and global crises. The world today is deeply divided, with tragedy all around. Understanding history goes hand in hand with standing up for truth and justice.”. Ai Weiwei. . . Explore. . Ai Weiwei | Dream Space . candidates.evidence_text: Wednesday 12 May 2027 – Band on the Wall Thursday 13 May 2027 – Southbank Centre Sona Jobarteh is the first professional female kora virtuoso to emerge from any of West Africa’s five Griot dynasties, and a singer, composer and bandleader whose concerts fill some of the world’s finest halls. In 2026 she sold out the Elbphilharmonie in Hamburg, played Munich’s Prinzregententheater and the Schleswig-Holstein Musik Festival, and on October 11 received the Silicon Valley African Film Festival’s 2026 Icon Award for her contributions to African music, scholarship and cultural promotion. On stage, Sona sings and plays the 21-string kora and guitar, joined by Eric Appapoulay, also on guitar, Andi McLean on bass, Yuval Wetzler on drums, Anselmo Neto on percussion and her son, Sidiki Jobarteh, on balafon. The show blends Mandé griot tradition with blues, Afropop and contemporary songwriting. She has also toured with blues legend Taj Mahal. Her concerts have become events wherever she plays. She has performed more than a hundred shows across Europe, Africa, the United States and beyond, in some of the world’s most prestigious theaters and festivals, with sell-outs at London’s Barbican, Cologne’s Philharmonie and the Seine Musicale in Paris, and appearances at the Hollywood Bowl, Symphony Space in New York and WOMAD Australia and New Zealand. Her latest album, Badinyaa Kumoo, was named one of the best albums of its year by Songlines Magazine, and her single “Gambia” has passed 32 million YouTube views. Recent collaborations include a feature on LL Cool J’s album The FORCE, on the song “Black Code Suite”, and a guest appearance on “Se a Vida Pede” from the Brazilian group Gilsons’ latest album. Born in London into a Gambian griot lineage of seven centuries, she began learning the kora at age three with her brother Tunde Jegede and father Sanjally Jobarteh; her cousin was the late Toumani Diabaté. She studied at the Royal College of Music, the Purcell School of Music and SOAS University of London. In 2015 she founded The Gambia Academy, which puts African history and culture at the centre of its curriculum, and she has keynoted forums hosted by the UN and the World Trade Organization. In 2023 Berklee College of Music awarded her an honorary Doctorate in Music alongside Usher and Roberta Flack

candidates.lead: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians.
candidates.evidence_text: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. Tickets from £13 per show, or £42 for a season ticket

candidates.evidence_text: We’re inviting young people to explore music for film and compose their own soundtrack this summer! Whether your child already attends our Saturday Music Club, or just wants to try something new, our Young Musician’s Summer School is suitable for all abilities! Across this 5 day course, we’ll be exploring music for film, and working on composing music for the silent film ‘A Trip to the Moon’. The course will conclude with a live performance soundtracking the film for family and friends. We welcome all abilities and instruments to take part in this course. You can bring your own instruments, but we have keyboards, guitars, bass, violins, drums and percussion on site which can be used if you don’t have an instrument. candidates.evidence_text: The Olllam is a band that fuses Irish traditional music with the modern jazz/post-rock energy of Detroit. Led by uilleann piper John McSherry, the band features Joe Dart (Vulfpeck), Michael Shimmin, Ross Ainslie, Seán O’Meara, and Joe Hettinga. Following their acclaimed album elllegy (RTÉ Radio 1 Best Group), The Olllam has collaborated with GRAMMY-nominated producer Zedd, shared the stage in Belfast with actor Anthony Boyle (Netflix’s House of Guinness), and recently completed a landmark U.S. tour in November 2025. From ancient airs to future soundscapes, The Olllam is not just carrying the tradition forward—they’re reinventing it

candidates.evidence_text: ГАРИК ОГАНИСЯН В ЛОНДОНЕ | 17 НОЯБРЯ | BIG BELLY COMEDY CLUB Tickets, Tuesday, November 17 • 7 PM - 9:30 PM | Eventbrite Share this event ГАРИК ОГАНИСЯН В ЛОНДОНЕ | 17 НОЯБРЯ | BIG BELLY COMEDY CLUB By UK STAND-UP CLUB Follow Big Belly Comedy Club Лондон, Greater London Tuesday, November 17 • 7 PM - 9:30 PM Overview Гарик Оганисян с новым стендап-концертом «Без негатива» Гарик Оганисян с новым стендап-концертом «Без негатива» Гарик Оганисян, один из самых ярких представителей современной русскоязычной стендап-сцены, приглашает вас на свой новый сольный концерт. Гарик известен как резидент Stand-Up Club #1, ведущий культового YouTube-шоу «Порараз Бирацца», участник проектов «Разгоны», «Книжный клуб», «Самый умный комик», «Стендап-комики», «Стендап Андеграунд». Кроме того, он является автором сольных концертов «Жизнь лучший драматург», «Жизнь худший драматург» и «И там, и сям» В новом концерте Гарик с присущими ему наблюдательностью, самоиронией и острым взглядом на происходящее расскажет о жизни, отношениях, эмиграции, повседневных абсурдах и обо всем, что превращает обычные ситуации в блестящую комедию. Не пропустите возможность провести вечер в компании одного из самых самобытных комиков своего поколения. Живой стендап, новые шутки и атмосфера, которую невозможно передать через экран. Хочешь, я приукрашу описание и добавлю несколько фактов? Например, Гарик был пятым участником группы the Beatles, но из-за природной скромности принял решение остаться в тени более пафосных коллег. Так же Гарик писал песни для групп Scorpions и Army of Lovers, является основателем гольф клуба в Майами, пробовал манго. Address: Big Belly Comedy Club, Unit 6 & 7, 30 Stamford St, London SE1 9LQ Doors: 19:00 Start: 19:40 Early Bird: £30 General Admission: £35 Late Bird: £40 18+ P.S. candidates.lead: Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been part of Manchester since 1867.
candidates.evidence_text: Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been part of Manchester since 1867. A £300,000 restoration, long-term lease and 23-year-old head chef are shaping what comes next Go to Manchester's Finest X profile Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been serving Manchester since 1867, but owner Roger Ward admits there was a point after Covid when he wasn’t sure how much longer he wanted to keep doing it Tom’s had gone eight years without a proper lease and much longer without any meaningful investment by the landlord. Retirement was being seriously considered. Instead, Roger decided to “go again properly” That decision has resulted in a new long-term commitment to the Chop Houses and around £300,000 being spent restoring Tom’s – touching everything from the dining rooms and furniture to the menu, wine list, kitchen and beer cellars Roger is particularly pleased with the toilets “Tom’s was famous for the shittest toilets in town,” he says. They are now, by his assessment, considerably less so. Downstairs has been redone, upstairs has new ones too, while a previously overlooked back room has been completely reworked

candidates.lead: Posted by Manchester Digital Introducing The Inside Track: A new way to get more from your Manchester Digital membership
candidates.evidence_text: Stay connected. Know what's next. We're launching The Inside Track , a new monthly online session designed to help Manchester Digital members stay informed, discover new opportunities and make the most of their membership Whether you've recently joined Manchester Digital or have been part of our community for years, The Inside Track is your chance to catch up with our team, find out what's happening across the network and explore ways to get more involved Taking place on the last Wednesday of each month, these free, members-only sessions will bring you up to speed on the latest developments, events and opportunities across Manchester Digital, all in just 30 minutes Each session will feature a topical focus, alongside practical updates on upcoming events, programmes, speaking opportunities and ways to raise your business's profile There'll also be time to ask questions, share your priorities and find out how we can help you get more value from your membership Our first edition at midday on 25th November will focus on some of the biggest opportunities coming up across the Manchester Digital community

candidates.evidence_text: Five days. Five themes. One city shaping its digital future. The first Manchester Digital Festival takes place from 8–12 February 2027 with its biggest and boldest programme yet. Manchester Digital has unveiled the programme for Manchester Digital Festival 2027 (MDF27 ) , bringin Taking place from Monday 8 to Friday 12 February 2027 , the festival marks an exciting new chapter for Manchester Digital, building on the success of Digital Skills Festival and expanding its scope to celebrate the full breadth of Greater Manchester's digital and technology secto The launch also comes as Manchester Digital celebrates its 25th anniversary , providing an opportunity to reflect on the people, businesses and innovations that have shaped the region's tech ecosystem, while looking ahead to what comes next With 15 events already announced and more to come, the first wave of the MDF27 programme offers everything from industry conferences and leadership discussions to careers events, founder stories and opportunities to explore emerging technologies Tickets for most events are now available , with further announcements expected in the coming months Under the banner Building our digital tomorrow , MDF27 introduces a new five-day format, with each day dedicated to a different theme reflecting the opportunities and challenges facing Greater Manchester's digital and technology sector

That depends who you ask… Tech by Chris Newbould November 4, 2026 Lecturers and students have significantly different perceptions of how much generative artificial intelligence (AI) is being used in university studies, according to new research from The University of Manchester and Spain’s Universidad del Pais Vasco/Euskal Herriko Unibertsitatea. The study found that academic staff perceived students to be using AI tools such as ChatGPT for their studies much more extensively than students reported themselves. Researchers say the findings highlight a gap in understanding between staff and students, at a time when universities are grappling with how best to respond to the technology. Academic staff rated their perception of students’ AI use at 5.23 out of seven, compared with an average of 3.11 among students reporting their own use for academic purposes. READ MORE: ANS Group reports 500% RoI from latest AI deployment Students were more positive than staff about the potential benefits of generative AI, including its ability to improve productivity, support learning and reduce workloads. The most prominent uses reported by students involved producing written text, finding answers to assignments, and translating or improving grammar. Staff varied considerably in their experience and expertise with AI, making it difficult for some to judge how students were using the technology. Researchers argue that universities need to move beyond treating AI primarily as a technical challenge or a threat to academic integrity, and develop a better understanding of how students and staff engage with it. The research examined how academic staff and students perceived their own use of generative AI tools, as well as their views of how the technology was being used in higher education. The study surveyed 45 academic staff and 86 students in a school covering social science disciplines at a UK research-intensive university. The questionnaires were conducted between April and June 2024, so essentially before AI took over the likes of Google whether you asked it to or not. When asked about students’ use of AI for academic purposes, staff gave an average rating of 5.23 on a seven-point scale. Students’ own responses produced an average of just 3.11. The researchers caution that students may have underreported their use of AI, but say the difference nevertheless points to the limited information staff may have about how students use these tools in their studies. AI use can be difficult for lecturers to identify, particularly when they see only the final version of an assignment rather than the process through which it was produced. Students may also use AI independently of their interactions with teaching staff, leaving academics with an incomplete picture of their working practices. The research also found that students were generally more positive than staff about the potential benefits of generative AI. Students rated the technology more highly in terms of its likely contribution to academic performance, including helping them learn about their subjects, increasing productivity and reducing workloads. They also felt more strongly than staff that appropriate conditions and support were in place to help them use AI tools. Among the uses identified in the survey, students reported using generative AI to find answers to questions and assignments, generate written work, and translate or improve the grammar of their writing. The researchers suggest that the immediate appeal of AI tools may lie in their ability to produce and improve text. However, they also argue that universities need to understand the range of ways students use the technology, rather than assume that its role in academic work is straightforward. The study also found considerable variation in staff members’ familiarity with AI. While 63 per cent of academic staff respondents had used at least one generative AI tool in the six months before the survey, some had limited practical experience of the technology. candidates.lead: A Manchester-based fintech company serving banks and specialist lenders has secured £1.5 million to automate the manual work that goes into preparing and assessing business loans, which limits how many deals lenders can take on and makes smaller loans to SMEs expensive to underwr
candidates.evidence_text: £1.5m boost as Manchester fintech brings automation to business loans - Prolific North Skip to content News Wise Owl gets another order of Our Farm Next Door News Data organisation appoints Vikas Shah Agency Reboot strengthens senior team £1.5m boost as Manchester fintech brings automation to business loans Tech by Chris Newbould November 4, 2026 A Manchester-based fintech company serving banks and specialist lenders has secured £1.5 million to automate the manual work that goes into preparing and assessing business loans, which limits how many deals lenders can take on and makes smaller loans to SMEs expensive to underwrite. Crediflow AI has developed a platform that pulls together the information credit teams currently gather and process by hand, such as financial statements, bank transactions and borrower documents, and turns it into structured credit analysis. The company uses AI to automate much of that work, which is typically spread across spreadsheets, PDFs, emails and other disconnected systems. Aggregating this data manually can sometimes take up to several days, but Crediflow says its platform reduces that time to between 10 and 30 minutes, giving credit teams more time to concentrate on critical tasks. READ MORE: Leeds financial tech consultancy merges with London cloud specialist In practice, the platform extracts and standardises figures from a borrower’s accounts, a process the industry calls financial spreading, analyses cash flow and drafts the memo a lender’s credit committee uses to approve a loan, in each customer’s preferred format. The platform is already used by hundreds of credit professionals across the UK, Europe and the US, supporting lenders of all sizes, from specialist lenders such as AddWorking Capital to global captive finance such as Iveco Capital. The round was led by NPIF II – PXN Equity Finance, which is managed by PXN Ventures as part of the Northern Powerhouse Investment Fund II (NPIF II), with investment also coming from Haatch and angel investors. The funding will accelerate development of the company’s platform, support engineering and product hires, and help Crediflow serve more banks and specialist lenders. Crediflow will also extend automation across the loan lifecycle, with workflows tailored to each lender’s credit policies and processes. By bringing origination, underwriting and monitoring together, Crediflow aims to reduce repeated work and help lenders grow their loan books without an associated increase in administrative costs. Last year, Crediflow became one of eight companies to receive funding from PXN’s PraeSeed programme, a 12-week cohort-based investment programme run in partnership with the British Business Bank and NPIF II to help scale early-stage businesses. Crediflow was founded by CEO Drey Kenfack, who has more than a decade of experience in commercial lending and private credit, including senior credit roles at Ford Credit Bank, DF Capital Bank and Advance Global Capital. Drey founded Crediflow after seeing first-hand how manual processes constrain lenders’ ability to grow. Drey Kenfack, CEO and founder of Crediflow AI, said: “Growing a loan book takes more than finding borrowers and having capital available. You need the capacity to assess those businesses, get decisions through approval and stay on top of risk once the money is out the door. I’ve spent much of my career doing that work. “When every transaction requires hours of manual preparation, it affects how much business a lender can take on and which deals are worth pursuing. We built Crediflow to bring that workload down and give credit teams more time to understand the borrower and structure the financing.” Joe Ball, senior investment associate at PXN Ventures , added: “Businesses of all sizes and across all sectors often rely on commercial finance for a multitude of reasons, but the processes involved in granting this finance are often largely manual, making the process inefficient and slowing down lending decisions. By automating this area of the sector, Drey and the Crediflow AI team are not just supporting lenders but also removing barriers for companies that need funding to grow.” Jonathan Keeling, partner at Haatch, said: “The best B2B founders build the product they wished they’d had in their last job. Drey spent over a decade in credit roles watching good deals stall on admin, and Crediflow turns hours of manual spreading and memo writing into structured analysis credit teams can act on.

The first season of parties is free, with guest list sign-up through the venue’s website, running Thursday to Saturday The core residents are Urbi, Shimrise, Groove Division, Joe Roche, Bay, SUI 13, Rhod Parry, Jacinta, Jordan Villa, Pez and Maclo, covering everything from Chicago and deep house to percussive Latin house, garage and acid

candidates.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained. Patrick Dorgu replaced Dalot, with Amad and Youri Tielemans also withdrawn, as Mason Mount and Shea Lacey came on The fifth and final change, with Ayden Heaven superseding Harry Maguire at half-time, saw Bryan Mbeumo substituted for Zirkzee himself. Так рождаются чувства, которые д Лондон — город, где встречаются десятки культур, языков и человеческих историй, где старинные набережные Темзы соседствуют с современными кварталами, а бешеный ритм мегаполиса не мешает беречь особую атмосферу уюта. В конце ноября именно здесь, вдали от дома, искренние композиции Концерты Дмитрия Волканова — это искренняя встреча, где между артистом и слушателями почти не остается дистанции. Стоит только прозвучать первым аккордам, как незнакомые люди начинают улыбаться друг другу, петь в унисон и чувствовать себя большой семьей, которую объединила музыка Когда к концу вечера Лондон окутает прохлада, сцена Studio 338 впервые встретит Дмитрия Волканова. candidates.evidence_text: Дронотур Бумбокса Європою. Листопад-грудень 2026 року. Презентація максі-синглу "Живий" Кожного разу, коли перед менеджментом гурту Бумбокс стоїть завдання написати пресреліз, ми починаємо згадувати цікаві факти. Скільки концертів зіграли, скільки грошей зібрали, які пісні видали. Це база. Непогано ще пам’ятати, чи був гурт у країні, до якої ми збираємося, чи це пер О, як би хотілося написати: "Концерт гурту Бумбокс" — і як у Львові за добу продано 8000 квитків. Так-так, ми не про Львів розповідаємо, хоча теж про Європу Наші віддані слухачі, якщо ви перебуваєте за кордоном, сподіваємось, вам буде цікаво дізнатися, що після традиційної перерви на декілька місяців, Бумбокс поїде в турне від Ізраїлю до Німеччини, від Англії до Польщі, від Ірландії до Словаччини та Чехії І повеземо ми в це турне свіженький, як херсонський кавун, максі-сингл “Живий”, підсилений піснями з різних альбомів, під частину яких виросли ви, а під частину зростають ваші діти Тож ознайомтеся, будь ласка, уважно з розкладом туру, купуйте квитки заздалегідь, готуйте гроші на донати та мерч — зустрінемося в листопаді

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Приготовьтесь к незабываемому вечеру с одной из самых любимых звезд турецкой поп-сцены — Муратом Далкылычем, в Лондоне! После выхода хита «Kasaba» в 2008 году Мурат Далкылыч стал одной из главных фигур турецкой поп-музыки. Он известен своим узнаваемым голосом, энергичными выступлениями и популярными песнями, среди которых «Bir Güzellik Yap». За годы карьеры в музыке, написании песен и кино он прио 29 января 2027 года Мурат Далкылыч выступит в indigo at The O2 в Лондоне. Вас ждет яркий вечер турецкой поп-музыки, живого исполнения и любимых хитов Не упустите возможность увидеть Мурата Далкылыча вживую в Лондоне!

Their plan is simple: to excite you, astound you and make you take stock of just how quickly this field is moving Expect a relaxed, afternoon of conversations about artificial intelligence, its ethics, the future of work and what might come next, alongside talks from people working at the cutting edge of AI If you're a technologist, business leader, students or just curious about AI, this is for you.
